identity.title: Complete remaining MVVM ownership boundaries after repository audit

origin.kind: 2026-08-19 owner-requested whole-repository MVVM audit and documentation handoff
origin.summary: The audit found that PL-0025 completed several concrete extractions but overclaimed repository-wide MVVM completion. The owner requested durable documentation before continuing with a lower-cost model.

state.current_summary: PL-0026 M1-M7 are complete: audited navigation, Shell smoke, Viewer recipe, Workbench execution, and Tool Lab responsibilities now have concrete owners; final Validation Set ownership and full qualification pass without changing product behavior.

objective.summary: Finish the remaining MVVM and maintainability boundaries with independently verifiable concrete owners while preserving public Viewer hosting and all explicit inspection-action contracts.
constraints: Preserve explicit Preview, Publish, Run, Validation, source/result separation, stable identities, and no-execution presentation actions.
Move responsibility and state to independent concrete owners; do not treat partial-file movement or delegating wrappers as completion.
Keep View code-behind limited to dialogs, WPF/OpenGL/pointer/docking adapters, and thin request wiring.
Use one lower-cost-model milestone at a time and split Viewer recipes and Workbench tool execution by coherent owner rather than attempting a big-bang rewrite.
Do not add a DI container, mediator, event bus, speculative interfaces, empty category folders, or a lib folder without an accepted DLL-only dependency.
Preserve the existing dirty worktree and do not commit or push without explicit owner authorization.

criteria.text: Owning documents and the issue ledger describe the audit correction, exact remaining owners, low-cost-model slice order, and non-overclaim completion rule.
Results and Validation navigation state and commands are owned by child ViewModels; the Views bind and render without directly mutating the screen state.
MainWindow retains WPF composition and callback wiring while command-line smoke scenario policy, capture helpers, and verification orchestration have independent Verification/Smoke owners.

Viewer recipe validation, load/apply, save, direct rule execution, and Preview orchestration are owned outside OpenVisionThreeDViewerControl while dialogs, rendering, pointer behavior, and public host compatibility remain intact.

Workbench execution state is split into independently testable concrete owners by coherent tool family, and ToolWorkbenchViewModel no longer directly owns each moved cancellation, running, stale, output, published, validation, and Tool execution path.
Repeated Tool Lab selected-step and window-lifecycle behavior has one bounded owner, and verification code uses explicit verification boundaries without changing supported smoke entry contracts.

Every milestone proves former-owner removal with focused checks and regression guards; final structure verification, Release build, diff hygiene, DLL policy, and required refreshed R0 validation pass.
